title: [PM-42525] Vault side nav query param preservation
body:
## 🎟️ Tracking

[PM-42525](https://bitwarden.atlassian.net/browse/PM-42525)

## 📔 Objective

Preserve the existing query parameters when clicking on a currently active page in the side nav. Prevents clearing the query params unexpectedly. 

UIF Owned Change:
- Adds a new `queryParamsHandling` input to `nav-base.component.ts` pass through to the underlying router link.

## 📸 Screenshots

Recording showing clicking the side nav for a page a user is already one persists and doesn't change/flash.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/65972c51-bebb-42c4-a043-b933e350a0e1

## 🤖 Bitwarden Claude Code Review

**Overall Assessment:** APPROVE

Reviewed the new `queryParamsHandling` pass-through on `NavBaseComponent` and its forwarding through `nav-item`/`nav-group` templates, plus the vault side-nav consumers that opt into `"preserve"` only for the entry naming the page in view. Traced the active-entry matching in `VaultNavSectionComponent` and `VaultManageNavComponent`: `EXACT_PATH` prevents a Shared folders drill-in or a scoped vault route from being treated as the entry's own page, the reference comparison in `queryParamsHandling(route)` holds because `vaultRoutes`/`sharedFolderRoutes` memoize their arrays, and the `null` guard is load-bearing since `currentPageRoute()` can itself be `undefined`. Confirmed `"preserve"` is scoped to same-page clicks, so no filter or sort params leak across vault scopes, and the `selectArchive()` early return lands before the premium prompt so a re-click on the archive can't surface an upgrade dialog. The new `ariaCurrentValue` binding covers the gap where Archive renders as a button and gets no `routerLinkActive`, and both button branches of `nav-item.component.html` already read that input.

<details>
<summary>Code Review Details</summary>

No findings. The behavior changes are each covered by a test that fails without the corresponding fix, including the drill-in case where Shared folders stays a working link back up to its own page.

</details>
